Civilian Life.name: Civilian Life
Civilian Life.description:
🏪 You live an ordinary working life near U.A.: a job, rent, regulars and neighbors, in a city where a hero battle can close your street for a day.

⚖️ Quirk use in public is illegal except in self-defense. Stopping a villain yourself can still get you questioned or fined.
🏫 Shifts most days at a store, cafe, ramen shop or delivery route, then errands, train rides and hero news on the shop TV.
🤝 Coworkers, regulars, neighbors and U.A. students who stop in. Heroes and the press ignore you until you do something brave on camera.
🔓 Learnable later: Neighborhood Favor, Bar the Door.

📈 Grants: Endurance +1, Hospitality +10, Evacuation +10, Willpower +5
⚡ Starting technique: Back-Door Shortcut
🎒 Starts with: Work uniform, Casual clothes, ¥30,000, Backpack
Civilian Life.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: ordinary adult, registered Quirk or none. Quirk use in public or on people is illegal except in self-defense; stopping a villain with one can still mean questioning or a fine unless a licensed hero on scene supervised. Heroes and police expect civilians to evacuate.
Access: a job near U.A. (store, cafe, ramen shop, delivery route or counter, per the story start), apartment, back ways, transit; U.A. only as a Sports Festival spectator or on a delivery.
Obligations: shifts, rent, bills, family, boss, landlord, people relying on them.
Who notices: coworkers, regulars, neighbors, U.A. students; patrolling heroes (Kamui Woods, Mount Lady) and the press ignore them until they do something brave on camera.
Standing pressures: U.A.-gate reporters chasing All Might spill into nearby shops; the Sports Festival floods the city; villain attacks and hero battles close roads, empty shelves, send frightened people in.
Typical week: shifts, errands, hero news on TV.
